meta.title: Ondra Zero-Residence Context
meta.description: Replaces resident text with deterministic pointers, where every hidden byte can be recovered verbatim (handbook §8.6, P1). The handbook gives one sentence: deterministic pointers replace resident content, every hidden byte is recoverable verbatim from the session log, and state is written to SQLite before compaction. This package turns it into four actions: compact splits a resident block into recoverable spans and hands back pointer text, recall fetches the original by pointer and verifies it, ledger lists the books (credentials only, never the prose itself), and fast is a pure preview that writes nothing and records nothing. Three judgements are hard-wired. First, a pointer is a function of content, not of time: the same block in the same session must yield the same pointer, otherwise every compaction rewrites the prefix and the prefix cache collapses. Second, compaction may only happen on a user-turn boundary, because rewriting the prefix mid-turn throws away that turn's cache. Third, no pointer is issued without a store: a pointer whose target could not be written is a link into nothing, so skipping this round is better than handing one out. Persona, worldbook and boundary blocks are never admitted — they are the frozen stable segment itself. Compared with summarisation it is reversible and auditable: the ledger records what was hidden, when, and how many characters, and a recall can be checked against its fingerprint. This package never takes over the message sequence, never assembles prompts, never calls a model and installs no timers; the replacement itself belongs to the dialogue orchestrator or the application shell.
